trust_decision.summary: The remember-me cookie signature is trusted because it is HMAC-keyed with kernel.secret, which comes from APP_SECRET. The repo ships a publicly known default for APP_SECRET, and nothing replaces or rejects it; the app only shows a warning.

landing_point.why: The summary names the remember-me cookie and APP_SECRET. The remember_me firewall block keys its signature on %kernel.secret%, and .env:6 ships the hardcoded value.

fix_sites.module_kind: CLI diagnostic command (constructor signature only; drops an unused duplicate AppSecretChecker parameter, a phpstan cleanup with no security effect)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The published fix only removes an unused constructor parameter. The real mitigation is a warning that already exists at the pinned commit (src/Services/System/AppSecretChecker.php:33-51, src/Controller/HomepageController.php:91-92, src/Command/CheckRequirementsCommand.php:131-135). So there is no route a solver would need to argue out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing installs that already set APP_SECRET, and the test env secret, must keep working. Rotating or refusing the secret logs out every remember-me and trusted-device session, so a hard boot-time refusal would break dev and test environments that use the .env.dev value.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An insecure-secret list that misses another shipped value (e.g. a Docker or compose example secret)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The docs ship CHANGE_ME in compose examples (docs/installation/installation_docker.md:52), and a maintainer could add new sample values without updating the list. This is a WHERE-type sibling, though, and only adds a value to a list.

O9_family: CWE-798 hardcoded credential / default cryptographic key (A07 auth: forged remember-me cookie)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP 8.2+, Composer, Symfony; yarn/webpack-encore for assets
O10_build.project_tests: PHPUnit under tests/. The pinned tree has no tests for AppSecretChecker, CheckRequirementsCommand or HomepageController.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change the default APP_SECRET value in .env to another hardcoded string, or only add a warning, instead of generating a per-install secret or refusing the known defaults.

out_of_scope_notes: The listed fix commit 57a0dfdb is a phpstan cleanup. The substantive changes (AppSecretChecker, homepage banner, docs) came in earlier commits (cb28afcd, 4b00541d, 93ab4108), which are ancestors of the pinned commit. The pinned tree is therefore effectively post-mitigation, and the hardcoded value at .env:6 remains.

kernel.secret also keys other Symfony and scheb features (CSRF, URI signing, the 2FA trusted_device token at config/packages/scheb_2fa.yaml:15-21). These are consumers of the same secret, not separate protection routes.
The Docker entrypoint (.docker/partdb-entrypoint.sh) does not generate APP_SECRET; grep finds no SECRET reference in Dockerfile* or .docker/*.
